The State Department offered up to $5 million for information, and the FBI issued an advisory on spotting such schemes.

5d2bba227ea31c26a295bca051517ab9d8c9d11e.summary: Sysdig Threat Research Team describes EtherRAT, a persistent Linux implant recovered on December 5, 2025 from a compromised Next.js application and linked to exploitation of CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell). It resolves its C2 address through Ethereum smart contracts, deploys five persistence mechanisms, and replaces its own code after first contact. The report notes overlap with DPRK-linked tooling but says attribution to a specific actor is unconfirmed.

5d5f2ab93acbd96631e9a6762effdcacbf94272c.summary: Cado Security blog post dated 21 December 2021 on a new version of a shell-script installer linked to the Abcbot botnet campaign. The script targets insecure cloud instances at cloud service providers such as Tencent, Baidu and Alibaba Cloud. It prepares hosts for compromise over SSH, kills processes of rival malware and miners, disables cloud monitoring agents, persists via rc.local and cron, changes iptables rules and propagates to known hosts. The authors link it to Abcbot based on code similarity and suggest a possible reference to TeamTNT. Trend Micro had reported an earlier version.

5d62961b48fedcdaf1993d4223f190fe64c29e35.summary: A DFIR write-up by Compass Security on a ransomware case. An ESXi hypervisor was encrypted by LockBit 2.0, after suspicious SSH logons traced to an end-of-life SonicWall SRA 4600 VPN appliance that was the initial entry point. The authors found an unauthenticated SQL injection that exposed cached VPN passwords, and a command injection in a bookmark feature that gave a reverse shell and root access.
